fields.meta_title: Solar Quote Form That Sizes Each System | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Create a solar quote form that turns monthly kWh use into a system size, flags older roofs for a site visit, and saves every request. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Solar Quote Form That Sizes the System From Usage
fields.hero_description: Build a solar quote form that sizes each system from kWh use, prices it per watt, and saves every request in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Solar Price Depends On
fields.features_subheading: Emergent turns your sizing math and price list into a solar quote form that puts a number on screen before the first call.
fields.feature_1:
System size from monthly kWh use

Set how many kWh a month one kW of panels covers in your area, and your price per watt. The form sizes the system from the usage and shows the estimate before anything is sent.
fields.feature_2:
Roof age and photos on every request

Ask for the roof material, its age, and photos taken from the yard. Set an age limit, and any roof older than that is held for a site visit, with no price on screen.
fields.feature_3:
Panel upgrades as their own line

Ask for the amperage of the main electrical panel. Set a price for each upgrade you install, and a home that needs one gets that line under the system price on its quote.
fields.feature_4:
Requests that reach the estimator

Email each request to the estimator who covers that area, with the usage, the roof answers, and the photos. The homeowner gets a copy of the quote by email once it is saved.
fields.feature_5:
A request board with overdue flags

Every request becomes a row in a database you own, with its system size and status. Pick how many days a request can wait for a site visit, and late ones are marked Overdue.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, exported to GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. A developer can place the quote form on the solar installer's own website and keep building on it from there.

fields.tab_content_1:
From 1,000 kWh a month, an 8 kW system priced at $24,800

Ines Halloway uses about 1,000 kWh a month, and she enters that and her address on Copperleaf Solar's form. Copperleaf counts 125 kWh a month for each kW of panels, and the form sizes her system at 8 kW. At $3.10 a watt, she sees a $24,800 estimate before she submits. Her request is saved with her answers.
fields.tab_content_2:
Calla checks each roof that is older than 15 years

Dunmore Solar Co. will not price a worn roof from photos. Wendell Arbuthnot uploads 3 roof photos of his asphalt shingle roof, which is 18 years old. Any roof older than 15 years gets a site visit before a price. The form shows him no number. Calla Renwick, the estimator, gets his request by email.
fields.tab_content_3:
On a 100-amp panel, Bettina's quote rises by $2,400

Bettina Molloy's house still has a 100-amp panel, and she says so on Saltgrass Energy's form. Her 7 kW system at $3.00 a watt comes to $21,000. Saltgrass adds a $2,400 panel upgrade to any home with a 100-amp main panel, and the form emails her a $23,400 quote that lists the system and the upgrade separately.
fields.tab_content_4:
Overdue after 2 days with no site visit on the calendar

Joaquin Ferrante runs sales at Kestrel Valley Solar, where the board lists 3 open requests. Any request older than 2 days with no site visit booked is marked Overdue and moves to the top. Hollis Teague asked 4 days ago and sits first. Mirela Stanhope's 1-day-old request is New, and Arjun Whitlow's visit is booked.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Solar Quote Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to put your sizing math, roof rules, and prices into a solar quote form, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Price the extras as separate lines
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull the last 20 systems you sold and write each home's monthly kWh use next to the system size you installed. Divide one by the other to find the kWh a month that one kW covered. That figure becomes the form's sizing math.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for usage in kWh, not dollars, because the sizing math runs on energy used rather than the amount paid. Add a short hint on where the number sits on the electric bill. A dollar field can stay as optional context for the first call.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide which roofs you will not price from a form. Pick an age limit, ask for the roof material, and require photos taken from the yard or the street. A roof past the limit goes to a site visit, and the form says that instead of showing a number.
fields.howto_step_4_des: List the work you add on top of the panels, such as a panel upgrade or a trench to a detached garage. Give each one its own question and its own price. The homeowner then sees what each extra adds to the system price.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the sizing figure, the price per watt, the roof rules, and the extras into one prompt. Emergent builds the solar quote form, the database behind it, and the request board. When the price per watt changes next quarter, type the new number into a prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide where each request goes. Priced requests can email the estimator for that area, and roof holds can go to whoever books site visits. Send the homeowner a copy of the quote too, with each line written out the way your sales team explains it.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it against a past quote
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run a test request for a house you already quoted by hand, then one with an old roof and one with a 100-amp panel. Compare each result with the number you gave, and adjust the sizing figure if a system comes out too large or too small.

faq_plan.q: What is a solar quote form?
faq_plan.a: A solar quote form is the request a homeowner fills in to get a price for panels. It collects the address, monthly electricity use in kWh, and details about the roof. A good one turns those answers into a system size and an estimate, or says that a site visit comes first.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a solar quote form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder: the questions, your sizing figure, your price per watt, and any roof or panel rules. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and a board for the requests. Test it with a few past jobs before you publish it.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a solar quote form ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the address, average monthly use in kWh, the roof material, the roof age, and two or three roof photos. Add the electrical panel's rating in amps, and ask if the person owns the home. Finish with a phone number and an email address for the follow-up.

faq_plan.q: Can a solar quote form estimate system size from monthly usage?
faq_plan.a: It can, with a figure from your own installs. Divide the homeowner's monthly kWh use by what one kW of your panels produced each month on past jobs. The form does that math as they type, much as a moving quote form turns home size into crew hours. Label the result an estimate, because the site visit can still change it.

faq_plan.q: Should a solar quote form ask for roof photos?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask for two or three photos taken from the ground, along with the roof material and its age. They let the estimator look for shade, vents, and worn shingles before the first call. With Emergent, each photo sits in a database you own, next to its request.

faq_plan.q: Should a solar quote form ask whether the person owns the home?
faq_plan.a: Yes, and put it near the top. If the person rents, show a short note asking them to share the page with the owner, and save the request with a Renter tag instead of sending it to the estimator. Owners go on to the usage and roof questions.

faq_plan.q: Should a solar quote form show a price before a site visit?
faq_plan.a: Only when the roof and the panel fit your rules. Show an estimate for roofs under your age limit, and hold the rest for a site visit with a plain note saying why. The same split works on a landscaping quote form, where a lawn gets a price and a retaining wall gets a visit.

faq_plan.q: Why ask about the electrical panel on a solar quote form?
faq_plan.a: Because a needed upgrade changes your price. Ask for the main panel's amperage, and add your upgrade price as its own line when the answer matches your rule, such as a 100-amp panel. The homeowner sees that line on the first quote instead of hearing about it at the site visit.

faq_plan.q: What happens after someone submits a solar quote form?
faq_plan.a: The request is saved and goes where you pointed it: an email to the estimator, or a hold for a site visit. A priced request also emails the homeowner the quote. Emergent builds the request board as well, and it marks a request Overdue once it passes the days you allow without a booked visit.

faq_plan.q: Can a solar quote form handle commercial rooftops?
faq_plan.a: Yes, with its own set of questions. Ask for the building type, the usable roof area in square feet, and the average monthly kWh use, then send those requests to a commercial estimator instead of showing a price. A construction quote form handles jobs too large to price online the same way.

plan.angle: The keyword has 20 searches a month, no ranked top 10 in the workbook, and an AlsoAsked tree about tax credits and house sizes that is all homeowner research, so the page wins on usefulness to the installer who builds the form: template pages stop at name, address and a notes box, which leaves the sales team to call back for usage and roof details. This page shows the answers that actually shape a solar price (monthly kWh use, roof age and photos, the main electrical panel) and what happens to a request after submit, across four jobs: an 8 kW system sized and priced on screen, an 18-year-old roof sent to the estimator for a site visit, a 100-amp panel upgrade added to an emailed quote, and a request board that marks requests Overdue when no site visit is booked within 2 days. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, the questions to ask, sizing from usage, roof photos, homeowners versus renters, price before a site visit, the electrical panel, follow-up, and commercial rooftops.
